sources.name: Johns Hopkins University, Sheridan Libraries -- JScholarship repository, 'Maps and Atlases' community, 'Maryland State, County and Baltimore City Atlases' collection
sources.access_note: Direct curl/requests fetches to jscholarship.library.jhu.edu get HTTP 403 (Cloudflare bot protection). All JHU URLs below were verified through a real browser session (Playwright over CDP). Item pages and metadata load fine once past the challenge; file downloads required in-page fetch() with credentials (see recipe below) because the bitstream '/download' and '/server/api/core/bitstreams/<uuid>/content' endpoints also sit behind the same Cloudflare check.
sources.license: No login required to view/download; items carry an 'Item-specific license agreed upon submission' (license.txt on each item) -- treat as free/open access digitized public-domain historical atlases, JHU-hosted. No paywall encountered.
sources.format: Individual plate scans as JPEG or JPEG2000 (JP2) or TIFF per item, no IIIF manifest observed, no GeoTIFF/tiles from JHU itself.

items.title: City atlas of Baltimore, Maryland, and environs: from official records, private plans and actual surveys (G.M. Hopkins, Jr.)
items.notes: This is THE core Hopkins 1876-77 Baltimore city atlas, JHU-hosted -- most directly useful single item for this project given the JHU institutional home.

Different content (contours/topography, not building footprints/ownership) but same era and large-scale; may be useful as a topographic base layer, not for parcel-level addressing.

items.notes: JHU also holds a small, JHU-property-specific Sanborn excerpt set (not the full-city LOC Sanborn collection). Not investigated further -- LOC's Sanborn holdings (see sanborn/manifest.json) are the comprehensive source; this JHU set only covers JHU-owned parcels.

sources.download_recipe: 1. Load the item page in a real browser (Cloudflare-protected). 2. Collect bitstream download links -- either the human link 'https://jscholarship.library.jhu.edu/bitstreams/<uuid>/download' or the direct asset 'https://jscholarship.library.jhu.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/<uuid>/content'. 3. Both are ALSO behind the Cloudflare check for bare curl/requests (confirmed: plain curl -I returns 403). 4. Within the same authenticated browser context, run page.evaluate with fetch(url, {credentials:'include'}) and pipe the arrayBuffer out (base64) to bypass the challenge, OR simply use the browser's native download (right-click/Save As) for one-off manual grabs. 5. For ~830 total items in the 'Maps and Atlases' community and hundreds of files per atlas, do NOT attempt an unattended bulk curl loop -- it will 403 immediately; any bulk pull needs a real, challenge-passed browser session (e.g. headless Chrome with a persistent context) driving the fetch loop, with pacing to stay polite to JHU's servers.

sources.name: Maryland State Archives -- 'bc_ba_atlases_1876_1915' scanned PDF series (Baltimore City & Baltimore County Atlases, 1876-1915, compiled by the late State Archivist Edward Papenfuse)
sources.access_note: These download with PLAIN curl, no browser/Cloudflare workaround needed, no login. http:// URLs 302-redirect to https://mdhistory.msa.maryland.gov, which then serves the PDF directly (HTTP 200).
sources.license: Public domain / state archives -- no login, no paywall encountered.
sources.format: One PDF per bound-atlas page/plate, sequentially numbered (-0001.pdf, -0002.pdf, ... at least through -0800.pdf confirmed to exist; did not probe beyond -0800 to avoid hammering the server). Each PDF appears to be a single-page raster scan (not a georeferenced GeoTIFF).
sources.scope: Confirmed spans at least the 1876 Hopkins city atlas and the 1896 Bromley city atlas (identified via cross-reference below), consistent with the collection's stated 1876-1915 range. Sheet-to-page-number mapping is NOT indexed anywhere I could confirm -- no finding-aid/TOC page was located (tried /html/index.html and several guessed msa.maryland.gov paths, all 404/403). Treat as a flat sequential scan run; would need manual browsing or the mdhistory.net site search (not accessed) to map a specific street/plate to a page number.
sources.how_found: Cross-referenced from mapwarper.net georeferenced-map metadata (see georeferenced section below), which recorded these exact PDF URLs as 'source_uri' for two already-warped Baltimore plates.

sources.caveat: This appears to be scattered, individual-user georeferencing (a handful of plates each from a few different atlas editions), not a systematic full-atlas georeferencing project. Coverage of any single edition is fragmentary -- do not assume the whole 1876 or 1896 atlas is tiled. Full list of all ~72 Baltimore-area entries on Map Warper (many unrelated to fire-insurance/property atlases, e.g. Lucas 1836, Warner & Hanna 1801) was captured separately by another research thread in this project (see data file already in scratch, not duplicated here since it is outside this task's Sanborn/Hopkins/Bromley scope).

sources.name: Archive.org
sources.result: NOT CONFIRMED. Searched archive.org's public advancedsearch API for 'Hopkins atlas Baltimore', 'Bromley atlas Baltimore 1906', and 'sanborn baltimore maryland' -- no relevant atlas or Sanborn map items found (only unrelated news-broadcast recordings and an unrelated 'Cecil County' atlas). Archive.org does NOT appear to independently host these Baltimore fire-insurance/property atlases; JHU JScholarship and the Maryland State Archives PDF series are the working sources, not archive.org.

sources.name: Historic Map Works
sources.result: NOT CHECKED -- WebSearch quota for this session was exhausted before this source could be investigated (see note below); site is a for-profit map-print vendor historically known to mirror low-res Hopkins/Bromley plate scans behind ads, typically NOT full-resolution or freely downloadable. Given strong verified free JHU + MSA coverage already in hand, deprioritized. If a georeferencing pipeline still needs it, check historicmapworks.com directly for a Baltimore-city browse page.

sources.result: NOT CHECKED for this task -- WebSearch quota exhausted (see note below) before this source could be investigated. The Baltimore City Archives' own online holdings are generally not full-resolution self-serve digitized atlases (much of their historic cartographic material has instead been digitized and redistributed via the MSA 'mdhistory.net' series found above, per Papenfuse's role as former State Archivist). Worth a follow-up WebFetch pass on baltimorecityarchives.org once search quota resets.
